summary: A three-screen Expo app. All habit data lives in one custom hook (useHabits) that loads from and saves to AsyncStorage; App.js owns simple navigation state (active tab + add modal) and passes data down to screens through props.

techStack.name: React Native + Expo
techStack.reason: Cross-platform UI from one codebase, with instant testing in Expo Go.

techStack.name: JavaScript (ES modules)
techStack.reason: Beginner-friendly and the language React Native is built on.

techStack.name: React hooks
techStack.reason: useState + useEffect inside a custom hook keep all habit logic in one place.

techStack.name: AsyncStorage
techStack.reason: Simple key-value storage that persists JSON on the device.

techStack.name: Custom tab bar + Modal
techStack.reason: Two tabs and one sheet don't need a navigation library — state is enough.

techStack.name: Ionicons (@expo/vector-icons)
techStack.reason: Crisp, familiar icons for tabs, checkmarks and buttons.

techStack.name: react-native-safe-area-context
techStack.reason: Keeps content clear of notches and the home indicator.

screens.name: Today
screens.purpose: The daily checklist: tick habits off and see today's progress.

screens.name: Progress
screens.purpose: Weekly overview: completion rate, check-ins, best streak and a 7-day grid.

screens.name: Add Habit
screens.purpose: A form to create a habit with a name, emoji and colour.

navigation.description: App.js stores activeTab and isAdding in state. The custom TabBar switches between Today and Progress, and a slide-up Modal shows the Add Habit form.

dataModel.description: A daily habit and the history of days it was completed.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Unique id (a timestamp) used as the list key.

fields.name: name
fields.description: What the habit is, e.g. "Read 20 pages".

fields.name: color
fields.description: Accent colour for the card and grid.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: The day the habit was added.

fields.name: completedDates
fields.description: Every day the habit was done; streaks are calculated from this.

stateManagement.description: One hook owns the habits array and exposes addHabit, toggleHabit and deleteHabit, so screens never modify data directly.

persistence.description: The hook loads the saved array on startup (falling back to sample habits) and saves the whole list whenever it changes.

architecture.description: Reusable UI pieces driven by props.
The single source of truth for habits.
Sample data and pure date helpers.
Colours, spacing and type used everywhere.

files.purpose: Design tokens: colours, habit palette, spacing, radius and type scale.
Pure helpers for date keys, the last 7 days and streak calculation.
Realistic sample habits generated relative to today.
Habit state, AsyncStorage persistence and the add/toggle/delete actions.
One habit row: emoji, name, streak and a check button.
Today's progress card with a percentage bar.
Custom bottom tab bar with Ionicons.
Daily checklist screen with a FlatList and add button.
Validated form for creating a habit.
Root component: habit state, tab navigation and the add modal.

buildSteps.title: Design tokens & date helpers
buildSteps.description: Define the look once, and write small pure functions for dates and streaks that everything else relies on.

buildSteps.title: Sample data & habit state
buildSteps.description: Create realistic seed data and the useHabits hook that loads, saves and updates habits.

buildSteps.title: Reusable components
buildSteps.description: Build the habit card, the progress card and the tab bar as prop-driven components.

buildSteps.title: The three screens
buildSteps.description: Compose components into the Today, Add Habit and Progress screens.

buildSteps.title: Wire everything in App.js
buildSteps.description: Connect the hook to the screens and add tab + modal navigation.

risks.risk: Saving before the first load finishes could wipe saved habits.
risks.mitigation: Only save after isLoading becomes false.

risks.risk: Time zones and midnight can make streaks off by one day.
risks.mitigation: Store local YYYY-MM-DD date keys instead of timestamps.

risks.risk: Corrupted storage could crash the app on launch.
risks.mitigation: Wrap JSON.parse in try/catch and fall back to sample data.

futureIdeas: Cloud backup so habits survive a new phone
